newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Phoenix weighing takeover bids.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Phoenix weighing takeover bids.

text.p: Danish roadbuilder Phoenix Contractors said on Thursday that it would take careful analysis to decide which -- if any -- of three bids for the company was the best for the business as a whole.

"Superfos' offer is best for the shareholders but we are looking for a holistic solution. We want to see what benefits shareholders, workers, the local community and Phoenix's own development," vice-chairman Ivan Hermansen told Reuters.
He did not rule out the possibility that more bids could emerge but did not identify any candidate.
Construction and chemicals group Superfos A/S offered on Thursday to pay 700 crowns per share for Phoenix A-shares, and 620 crowns for the most-traded C-share.

The offer trumped an earlier bid by Norway's Rieber and Son but was later outdone by small provincial Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen which offered 710 crowns per A-share and 625 crowns per C-share.

The Copenhagen bourse put Superfos, Phoenix and Pedersen on its list of shares marked for special observation, standard procedure when a share is more than usually active due to special circumstances.
Phoenix's Hermansen said that he might advise shareholders to ignore all bids and let the company carry on as an independent entity.
"That is also a possibility, although the higher the bids are, the greater the demands on the Phoenix board and management if we think we can be independent," he said.
Dealers welcomed the open nature of the bidding, a first in Denmark where mergers and takeovers traditionally become public only after they have been agreed.
"Bids are not announced in public but normally negotiated discreetly in the wings," an analyst at a leading bank said.

"Today was a historic day in that sense... there is no raider culture in a little country like this such as there is in the Anglo-Saxon world ...there are signs though that a more aggressive style is on its way here as pension funds become more dynamic," he told Reuters.
He believed that Superfos, one of the top-20 companies listed on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange was by far the best suitor for Phoenix.
"There is little doubt that Superfos and Phoenix would clearly be the best synergy. it is obviously the best thing for Superfos to take over Phoenix. Pedersen is simply too small."
Phoenix's C-share closed at 620 crowns, a hefty 30 crowns up from Wednesday's close while Pedersen rose 50 crowns to 2,250.
Superfos rose a more modest 15 crowns to 785 crowns. Its Phoenix bid, worth a total 767 million crowns is open until March 3.
